expect_red: fitSphere recovers a sphere exactly, and refuses a plane rather than guessing a centre somewhere behind it

mutations.contract: A point set that does not determine a sphere gets `null`, never a pseudo-solution. A guessed centre leaves this file as a joint location in an assembly frame, and nothing downstream can tell it was guessed.
mutations.note:
The mutation nudges a singular pivot to a tiny non-zero instead of refusing, which is the shape of the fix somebody reaches for when a solver 'randomly returns null'. Applied, a flat 4x4 grid of points comes back as a sphere centred in its own plane with a radius of 1.58 -- finite, plausible, and entirely invented.
Two earlier mutations here were NOT witnessed and the reason is worth keeping. Removing the singularity test outright leaves the elimination dividing by a pivot of ~0, the radius comes out NaN and the `r2 > 0` test below still returns null; removing THAT test instead leaves the pivot test returning null first. The refusal is two tests deep, and only a mutation that produces a FINITE wrong answer gets past both -- which is also the only version of this bug a consumer could not notice.
